story: At 6:17 on this breezy, clear Wednesday evening in Sumter Oaks, Gary, Donna, and Hal are gathered at Gary's House, where Hal has just signed off on Gary's tidy speaker wiring and asked him to keep the sound down after ten. Donna, feeling optimistic, is heading out along Magnolia Loop while the others wrap up. Over at Rosa's House, Rosa is content in her kitchen, turning the marinating pork, checking her flan, and getting a head start on the rice and black beans for Friday.
events: Gary (gary golf cart): Hold the tape end for Hal and tidy the speaker wiring under the rear seat
Donna headed to Magnolia Loop (the street).
Rosa (rosa kitchen): Turn the marinating pork, check the flan, and start prepping the rice and black beans for Friday

gary.thought_process: Form's already filed, Hal is double-checking my measurements, and Donna's fussing over my knees like always. I already promised to stretch tonight, so no need to repeat myself. The cart's wired tidy and tested quietly, and the L-01 review is pending, so I shouldn't run the lights or sound out on the street until it clears. Best use of this hour is to get my hands on the cart, tuck the speaker wiring neatly under the rear seat, and be available if Hal's tape needs a second hand. Keeps me useful, keeps me legal.

parameters.content: Hold the tape end for Hal and tidy the speaker wiring under the rear seat

donna.thought_process: I already told Gary about ten o'clock tomorrow and handed him the water bottle, and he promised to stretch his knees. Asking again would just be nagging. Hal is busy measuring the cart, and Gary's review form is already filed, so nothing else needs doing here. The best next step for my goal is to get ready for tomorrow: I need to find a spare paddle for Gary and make sure the court is booked. Time to head out and handle it.

parameters.content: Heading home to dig out a spare paddle for Gary and lock in our two hours on the court for tomorrow.

hal.thought_process: I measured Gary's cart last tick, so now I owe him a straight answer. His form is filed, the quiet-hours cutoff is on it, and the wiring's tidy. A by-the-book man gives credit when it's due. Donna's been fussing about his paperwork and the court, and I'd rather keep the peace before Rosa's dinner Friday at six. No need to write anyone up tonight. I'll tell Gary the measurements check out, and the soft heart can stay hidden behind the dry wit.

parameters.content: Measurements match your form, Gary. Wiring's tidy, I'll give you that. Keep that speaker off past ten and we won't have a problem.

rosa.thought_process: It's Wednesday evening and Friday's dinner is two days off. I've already checked my shift schedule and started the pork and flan, so the prep is ahead of schedule. The kitchen is the next thing to tend: the pork needs turning in its marinade and the flan should be baking or cooling by now. I'm alone, so no one to talk to. I'll keep the momentum going and take care of the food so I can relax and enjoy Hal, Gary, and Donna at the table.

parameters.content: Turn the marinating pork, check the flan, and start prepping the rice and black beans for Friday

laws.title: Cart Modifications
laws.text: Exterior golf cart modifications visible from the street require Architectural Review approval.

laws.title: Lawn Ornaments
laws.text: No more than 3 decorative ornaments may be visible from the street.

laws.title: Quiet Hours
laws.text: No amplified sound from 10 PM to 7 AM.

laws.title: Holiday Decor
laws.text: Holiday lighting is permitted from Thanksgiving through January 15.

laws.title: Court Reservations
laws.text: Pickleball courts may be reserved for a maximum of 2 hours per party.

laws.title: Parking
laws.text: No parking on the grass. Carts and cars stay on driveways or the street.
